concerns.text: T004b enforces strict exit-1 on DATASET_URL/DATASET_DOI mismatch at runtime, violating Constitution Principle I ('fetched from same canonical source on every run'). A valid source update (e.g., Zenodo version bump) halts the entire pipeline. This creates a brittle single point of failure incompatible with 'fresh run' reproducibility.

T020 (Westfall-Young permutation correction, n=10000) is listed as strict prerequisite for T017 (dimension classification), but spec.md US1 Acceptance Criteria only requires 'Pearson and Spearman correlations with confidence intervals'—no multiple-comparison correction is mandated. This introduces unrequested statistical complexity (scope creep) without corresponding FR/SC justification.

T041 requires validation on 'n ≥ 30 subset' but spec.md US1 does not specify minimum sample size for this gate. Arbitrary threshold of 30 lacks justification in spec/plan, risking gate passing on statistically insignificant data or failing on valid small-sample datasets. Violates 'Verified Accuracy' principle of traceable thresholds.

T024 calculates projected hours via simple linear extrapolation (mean_time * sample_size / 3600), but spec.md US2 requires 'Linear scaling projection'. Task description does not verify linearity assumption (R² check) before projecting. T021b (Scaling Validation) is placed AFTER T024 in dependency chain, creating logical flaw: projection generated on potentially non-linear data before validation confirms linearity.

T012 and T013 specify returning 'zero vector' for missing audio/optical flow, but spec.md does not define how missing data impacts 'feature-sufficient' classification. Zero-filling may artificially inflate/deflate dimension correlations, invalidating resulting 'VLM-required' or 'feature-sufficient' flags. Violates Data Hygiene requirement for documented missing-data handling.

T028 generates 'Long-format CSV' for sensitivity matrix, but spec.md SC-004 only requires 'Methodological verification (sensitivity matrix)' without specifying format. While long-format is valid, lack of explicit format definition in spec creates risk of misalignment with downstream paper generation or review tools, requiring potential rework.
